findings.summary: finishNavigation() uses stale CSS class selector '.bce-item-row' which does not exist in the new Blueprint-based ItemList; focus() silently fails, leaving keyboard focus unset after folder navigation completes
findings.failure_scenario: User navigates to a subfolder. After items load (percentLoaded === 100), finishNavigation() calls focus(this.rootElement, '.bce-item-row'). The new ItemList renders rows with class 'be-ItemList-item', not 'bce-item-row', so no element is found and focus is lost. Users must click or tab manually to interact with the list.

findings.summary: closeModals() uses stale CSS class selector '.bce-item-row-${focusedRow}' which does not exist in the new Blueprint-based ItemList; focus restoration after closing a modal silently fails
findings.failure_scenario: User opens a modal (rename, share, delete, etc.), closes it, and closeModals() tries to restore focus via focus(this.rootElement, '.bce-item-row-3'). The new ItemList does not produce 'bce-item-row-N' classes; focus is not restored and the user is left in an unfocused state.

findings.summary: Keyboard arrowdown handler introduces a 'document.activeElement &&' guard in grid view that prevents focusing the first item when no element is currently focused (activeElement is null), a regression from the old isFocusOnItem() behavior
findings.failure_scenario: Page loads fresh, nothing is focused (document.activeElement is null). The old code's isFocusOnItem() returned false (via !undefined === true), triggering focus on the first item. The new code evaluates 'null && ...' as falsy, so nothing happens on arrowdown. User must click or tab before keyboard navigation works.

findings.summary: Keyboard arrowdown handler introduces a 'document.activeElement &&' guard in list view that prevents focusing the first item when no element is currently focused, same regression pattern as the grid-view case
findings.failure_scenario: Same as above but for list view: pressing arrowdown with nothing focused does nothing, whereas the old code unconditionally focused the first row and set focusedRow to 0.

findings.summary: getElementBySelector() calls itself recursively instead of calling getElementsBySelector(), causing a stack overflow when invoked
findings.failure_scenario: Calling helpers.getElementBySelector('.be-ItemList-item') or helpers.getListItemByIndex(0) triggers infinite recursion: getElementBySelector calls this.getElementBySelector(selector) which is itself. Stack overflow crashes the test runner.

findings.summary: Duplicate test blocks: two identical tests named 'renders component with correct columns for medium screen devices' at lines 41 and 50, likely an unintentional copy-paste
findings.failure_scenario: The same assertions run twice, wasting test execution time. No behavioral impact, but the duplicate suggests the second block may have been intended to test a different scenario (e.g., 'shoulder render grid view mode' was also a copy-paste typo fixed in the same PR).

findings.summary: ContentProps.focusedRow is declared as a required prop but is never destructured or used in the component body after the refactor; ContentExplorer still passes it but it is silently dropped
findings.failure_scenario: The focusedRow value, which ContentExplorer sets when a user clicks an item or presses arrowdown, no longer reaches the ItemList component (the old react-virtualized Table used it for scrollToRow). Keyboard-based row tracking is broken, and scroll-to-focused-row no longer functions.
